title: Monotonicity of reachable-code counts
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary input, and let $s$ be a nonnegative integer. For each $t$, let $R_t$ be the set of natural numbers below $2^{K(N)(t+ loor{ rac{\log_2 |x|}{1}}+2)}$ that can be reached from the code of the initial configuration on $x$ by zero or more encoded machine steps that stay within work-tape window $t$, where $K(N)$ is the fixed code-length parameter of $N$. Then $|R_s|\le |R_{s+1}|$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite-state nondeterministic machine $N$ over binary alphabet
